title: An ex vivo cornea infection model
author: Ubani-Ukoma, Chauhan, et al.

steps.title: Prepare agar media and broth
steps.instruction: Dissolve 18 g TSB and 3 g granulated agar in 600 ml 18.2 MΩ deionized water, stir with a magnetic stirrer to make soft agar; dissolve 24 g TSA powder in 600 ml water for TSA plates; dissolve 18 g TSB powder in 600 ml water for broth. Autoclave all solutions on the liquid cycle for 30 min (or 45 min) at 121 °C. After autoclaving, add fluconazole to the soft agar to a final concentration of 21.25 µg ml⁻¹, then pour the agar into sterile 90 mm Petri dishes.

steps.title: Culture bacterial pathogens
steps.instruction: Streak each pathogen (P. aeruginosa PAO1, S. aureus SA35556) onto TSA plates and incubate 16–18 h at 37 °C. Inoculate 5 ml sterile TSB in a 15 ml tube with a single colony, vortex, and shake overnight at 150 rpm, 37 °C. Transfer 0.2–0.5 ml of this overnight culture into 20–30 ml TSB in a 250 ml flat‑bottom flask, shake at 150 rpm, 37 °C for 2 h (or until the optical density at 640 nm reaches 0.2–0.4, corresponding to ~10⁸ CFU ml⁻¹ in a 1 cm cuvette).

steps.title: Dissect frozen rabbit corneas
steps.instruction: Obtain whole frozen rabbit eyes and keep them frozen. Hold the eye with a gloved hand or place it in a polystyrene tray (15 mm conical‑tube wells) lined with gauze so that roughly half of the globe is above the surface; secure any movement with dissecting pins. While the globe is still mostly frozen, warm the cornea slightly with a thumb or finger. Create a central partial‑thickness wound using a sterile 8 mm punch biopsy, trephine, or vacuum trephine. Dissect the corneal button away from the globe with a crescent knife, forceps, or blunted needle; cut remaining attachments with curved tenotomy scissors or a crescent knife; excise the cornea with a scleral rim using a sterile disposable scalpel; peel off the iris and ciliary body with forceps. Store the excised corneas in an airtight container at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: Disinfect corneas with povidone‑iodine
steps.instruction: Place groups of six corneas into sterile 50 ml tubes. Add 35 ml of 10 % povidone‑iodine (PI) and incubate 30 min at room temperature. Decant the PI and rinse by adding 35 ml sterile PBS, vortex, and repeat the PBS rinse at least five times or until no visible PI remains. Use the corneas immediately in the next step.

steps.title: Embed corneas in soft agar and inoculate
steps.instruction: Position each cornea epithelial side down in a sterile mold and fill the surrounding cavity with sterile soft agar. Allow the agar to solidify (≈10 min; confirm by gently touching the surface with a sterile pipette tip or swab). Transfer the corneas epithelial side up onto sterile soft agar plates (maximum three corneas per plate). Spot the injury site with 1 µl of pathogen suspension (10⁸ CFU ml⁻¹) or 1 µl PBS as a control. Replace the lid and incubate the plates at 37 °C for at least 2 h (acute infection) or longer as required by the experimental design.

steps.title: Apply treatments and harvest samples
steps.instruction: Within a biosafe hood, apply experimental contact lenses or other topical treatments to each plate; remove lids only inside the hood. At each predetermined time point, remove the lenses, excise the injured area and surrounding cornea with a sterile 12 mm punch biopsy, peel the agar from each corneal button, and transfer each button into a separate sterile 15 ml tube containing 7 ml PBS‑Tween (PBS‑T). Vortex the tubes multiple times.

steps.title: Quantify viable bacteria
steps.instruction: Perform at least four successive ten‑fold serial dilutions of each suspension. Plate each dilution on TSA plates using either standard streaking or a spiral plater. Incubate the TSA plates 16–18 h at 37 °C, count colonies, and calculate CFU ml⁻¹. Optionally, capture images of the corneas and prepare hematoxylin & eosin‑stained sections for histological assessment.

steps.title: Screen antiseptic candidates
steps.instruction: For each candidate antiseptic, place groups of five corneas in sterile 50 ml tubes and submerge in 35 ml antiseptic solution for 30 min at room temperature. Include a negative control (35 ml PBS) and a positive control (35 ml 0.85 % NaOCl) under identical conditions. Decant and rinse each cornea with 35 ml sterile PBS, vortex, and repeat the rinse at least five times until no antiseptic is visible. Image the corneas to assess tissue integrity and discard agents causing extensive damage. Transfer each rinsed cornea to a 15 ml tube containing 5 ml TSB, shake overnight at 37 °C, 150 rpm. The following day, assess broth turbidity visually and measure absorbance spectrophotometrically.

steps.title: Validate sterilization with infection assay
steps.instruction: For antiseptics that passed screening, place corneas face down in a sterile mold, fill with agar, and inoculate with 1–5 µl of pathogen at 10⁸ CFU ml⁻¹. Incubate 16 h at 37 °C. After incubation, collect the injury site and peripheral cornea with a 12 mm punch biopsy, separate the agar, and submerge the corneal button in 7 ml PBS‑T. Vortex five times, then sonicate in a bath for 90 s, pause 60 s, and repeat for a total of five cycles. Centrifuge the suspension, collect the pellet, extract genomic DNA, and submit the sample for 16S rRNA sequencing to confirm that the recovered bacteria match the inoculum.

description: IMPORTANT: All steps within this method should be carried out using aseptic technique in a biosafe hood.
